exposure: Prior arrest of progression (disaggregated into prior arrest of dilatation and prior arrest of descent)
outcome: Prediction of vaginal birth after cesarean (TOLAC) success
cohort: 989 women who underwent trial of labor after cesarean (TOLAC) deliveries from a tertiary academic medical center between February 2017 and December 2018
finding: All three machine learning models (random forest, regularized regression, and eXtreme gradient-boosted decision trees) outperformed the MFMU model in predicting TOLAC success, with the XGBoost model requiring only eight variables for accurate prediction.
